title: Ordinary singleton left extension
statement:
For any index n, the ordinary left adjoint to strict evaluation at n has level m equal to B_m tensor over B_n with P when m≤n, and zero otherwise. It is additive, has its natural tensor comparison below n and vanishes above n. The ordinary Hom transpose at a lower level is the evaluated map preceded by the inverse tensor comparison, and equals the original evaluation-adjunction transpose followed by the strict transition.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (T : SystemTensorCoherence S)
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (n : ℕ)
theorem systemSingleTranspose {m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) (P : systemLevel B n)
    (M : StrictRingSystem B) (f : (systemSingleFunctor S T B n).obj P ⟶ M) :
    (systemTensorAdj S B h).homEquiv P (M.level m)
      ((systemSingleBelow S T B n h).inv.app P ≫ f.app m) =
    (systemSingleAdjunction S T B n).homEquiv P M f ≫ M.transition h
```

proof.text: Construct the tensor transition below n by scalar adjunction and the canonical associator, and use the unique zero map in the remaining cases. Tensor generators and the ring functor composition law prove the system laws. At n the inverse tensor unit supplies the adjunction unit. Given P→M_n, take its composite with each transition and scalar-transpose it below n, and use zero above n. The strict composition law proves the system-map equations. Transposing at n and checking tensor generators proves the inverse Hom identities; componentwise tensor additivity proves additivity.
